title: One tea brief, four models
scenario:
You design launch assets for a small tea shop. Its new jasmine tea is called Jasmine Hush. Your teammate wrote first prompts for four image models and noted what came back.

Use the exhibit. The shop, the prompts and the notes are made up for this case. The model names are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
DRAFT PROMPTS AND RESULTS (made up)

  Ideogram 4.5
    Prompt: "Poster for Jasmine Hush tea, pale stone, gold rim tin --ar 16:9 --style raw"
    Result: a square image; the poster shows the letters "--ar 16:9" in a corner.

  FLUX 3 Image
    Prompt: "Tea tin on a table, no people, no clutter, no text"
    Result: a busy cafe table with two cups and a menu card.

  Recraft V4.1 (model: recraftv4_1)
    Prompt: "Jasmine Hush tin icon, brushed metal texture, soft reflections"
    Result: a PNG photo-like icon. The web team asked for an SVG file.

  Ideogram 4.5 (second try, settings left at their defaults)
    Prompt: "A tin labelled \"Jasmine Hush\" on pale stone"
    Result: the prompt shown under the image is three times longer and adds a teapot, steam and a garden.

questions.prompt: Ideogram: the image came back square, with "--ar 16:9" printed on it. What is the best fix?

options.text: Move --ar 16:9 to the very start of the prompt so it is read first
options.explanation: Ideogram does not read flags like --ar as commands at all. It treats them as words, wherever they sit.

options.text: Write the flag twice, as --ar 16:9 and --aspect 16:9, to be safe
options.explanation: Both are still words to Ideogram. More flag text gives the model more letters it may draw.

options.text: Delete the flags and pick 16:9 in the Image app's aspect ratio setting
options.explanation: Right. Ideogram treats flags like --ar as words and says to set aspect ratio in the Image app settings.

options.text: Keep the flags and add "no text in the corners" to the end of it
options.explanation: The ratio is still not set, and the flags stay in the prompt as words to draw.

questions.prompt: FLUX 3 Image: the "no people, no clutter, no text" prompt gave a busy cafe table. Which rewrite fits FLUX's guide best?

options.text: Tea tin on a table, absolutely no people, no clutter, no text at all
options.explanation: FLUX 3 Image has no negative prompt field. Stronger "no" words are still negatives.

options.text: A single tea tin alone on a bare pale stone table, unmarked surfaces
options.explanation: Right. FLUX's guide says to replace each negative with what you would see there, such as "empty", "solitary" or "unmarked".

options.text: Tea tin on a table, and send "people, clutter, text" as a negative prompt
options.explanation: FLUX's page says FLUX 3 Image has no negative prompt field.

options.text: Tea tin on a table, keep the same words, then run it ten more times
options.explanation: The prompt still asks with negatives. Running it again leaves the result to chance.

questions.prompt: Recraft: the web team needs the icon as an SVG file. What should change?

options.text: Keep recraftv4_1 and add the words "SVG file" to the end of the prompt
options.explanation: On Recraft the model name decides the output: names without _vector produce raster images.

options.text: Use a _vector model and describe shapes, two colours and an even stroke
options.explanation: Right. Recraft model names ending in _vector produce SVG, and its V4 guide says to define shape, colour and line, not texture.

options.text: Use a _vector model and keep "brushed metal texture, soft reflections"
options.explanation: The model is right, but Recraft's V4 guide says to avoid texture or material language for vector work.

options.text: Keep recraftv4_1 and ask for a higher quality setting for sharp edges
options.explanation: A raster model still makes a raster image. The web team asked for an SVG file.

questions.prompt: Ideogram, second try: the prompt was rewritten and a teapot and a garden were added. The client wants exactly the tin and the stone. What do you do?

options.text: Turn Magic Prompt off so Ideogram follows your exact words this time
options.explanation: Right. Magic Prompt rewrites and expands prompts and starts on. The Ideogram docs say to turn it off when you want your exact words followed.

options.text: Leave Magic Prompt on and add "no teapot, no garden" to the prompt
options.explanation: The rewriter can still expand the prompt, and Ideogram's guide prefers saying what you want over "no".

options.text: Switch to Ideogram 3.0 and list "teapot, garden" as a negative prompt
options.explanation: Magic Prompt is also on Ideogram 3.0, and it starts on there too. The rewriter is the cause.

options.text: Make the prompt three times longer so the rewriter has less to add
options.explanation: No source here says a longer prompt stops Magic Prompt. The toggle is the direct control.
